text:
maria: Heads up — saw a perf regression on main after yesterday's kernel-choice heuristic tweak. Token latency p50/p95 up ~7-12% on p4d runs. NSYS shows CPU-side spinups in the handoff path. Attaching quick notes.

jon: Ugh. Is this in batching coordinator or KV cache path? Any perf/stack dumps?

maria: Quick perf capture and a tiny collapsed stack from one hot thread (nsys + perf sampling):

```
perf record -F 99 -g -- ./run_infer --profile 1000
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```

Sample stack (collapsed lines):
```
BatchCoordinator::try_handoff;Batcher::pop_batch;PyEval_EvalFrameEx;tokenize_chunk;memcpy
BatchCoordinator::try_handoff;futex_wait;__pthread_cond_wait;__poll;syscall
```

maria: The odd bit is a bunch of futex/syscall wakeups during small handoffs — not the GPU kernel time. GPU kernels look identical in nsys. CPU spin/net wake cost seems to balloon when batcher sizes are small and kernel choice prefers non-blocking copy path.

kevin: Could be the new threshold forces more CPU-side copying instead of letting the kernel handle contiguous IO. Did you check context-switches/voluntary context-switches?

maria: Ran perf stat on same workload: ``perf stat -e context-switches,cs,task-clock,cycles,instructions -p <pid>``

Output summary (diff vs baseline):
```
context-switches: +42k
task-clock: +9%
cycles: +11%
instructions: +3%
```

jon: context-switches x42k is huge. That aligns with futex wakeups. Which code path changed in the heuristic? Is it choosing kernel variant A -> B for short seq lengths?

maria: Yes. New heuristic switches to "nonblocking-shared" kernel for <64 token leftover to reduce latency on small tails. That seems to cause more frequent KV handoffs and micro-batches.

kevin: Two quick hypotheses: 1) increased handoff freq => more thread wakeups + futex contention; 2) nonblocking path does many small memcpy calls on CPU due to alignment/stride, causing higher syscall/wake overhead. Could add a short backoff/yield in handoff loop. Try sched_yield or nanosleep(100us) when handoff tries > N.

maria: I'll try inserting an exponential backoff starting at 50us after 3 failed handoff attempts. Also going to run a variant that forces the old blocking kernel to confirm.

qa-bot: Regression test run 2170012350: small-tail workload 1000 iters. baseline=85ms p95, main=96ms p95, pinned-blocking-kernel=86ms p95. Attach logs: https://ci/internal/2170012350/log
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 0.12.4 -> 0.12.5 started for eng-runtime/p4d-cluster :rocket:

jon: Good call to test pinned-blocking kernel. If that fixes it, we can either revert heuristic or change threshold up. Also add histograms for handoff attempts count per request so we have telemetry.

kevin: For instrumentation, add counters: handoff_attempts, handoff_spin_total_time_ns, handoff_yield_count. That will let us alert when handoff time spikes.

maria: Agreed. I'll push a small patch with backoff + counters to the branch and run perf/NSYS again. If backoff reduces context switches and task-clock goes down ~8-10% we call it a win. Will post updated flamegraph.

jon: One more ask — capture a perf script sample with --call-graph dwarf so we can see Python frames more clearly; current folded stacks show PyEval_EvalFrameEx which is noisy.

maria: On it. Also will include a small perfetto timeline slice focusing on CPU threads during a 60s steady window. NSYS showed the GPU idle/wait overlap but CPU is the cause here. cc @kevin for follow-ups. :eyes:

kevin: Thanks. If backoff works, consider also tuning the kernel-choice threshold upward by a few tokens (maybe 96) and retest at scale.

maria: Patch pushed to branch/hand-off-backoff, running CI + perf now. Will update with flame.svg and perf stat diffs in this thread. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary 0.12.5 rolled out to 3 nodes; monitoring...
